title: Route-aware Cost Guardian: per-customer batching/caching prescriptions, allowlist/denylist, and failsafe rollback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Build a route-centric "Cost Guardian" that generates per-customer and per-route batching/caching prescriptions, enforces tier-based allowlists/denylists, and applies changes via a safe canary+rollback flow. Background: we've seen variable token costs and tail latency driven by a small fraction of routes and tenants; coarse global heuristics waste capacity and expose customers to quality regressions when aggressive batching/caching is applied. This ticket scopes an automation layer that: 1) segments routes and tenants by workload shape and SLA tier; 2) produces human-reviewable prescriptions (batch sizes, KV cache prefixes, TTLs, and quantization suggestions) with rationale and expected unit-cost delta; 3) enforces allowlist/denylist constraints (e.g., high-SLA customers must be denylisted from aggressive batching that increases p95); and 4) performs a guarded apply with dry-run, canary rollout, monitoring windows, and automatic rollback triggers. The implementation will integrate telemetry signals (p50/p95 latency, error rate, quality-check fail-rate, token spend delta) and use runtime-1.22 rollout hooks to orchestrate safe applies. We will provide a Console UI view for recommended prescriptions and an API to accept/reject and schedule applies. Work includes: recommendation engine prototype, policy engine updates (allowlist/denylist + tier maps), canary orchestration, rollback detector, and e2e tests with synthetic traces.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine produces per-route, per-customer prescriptions (batch_size, cache_ttl_ms, kv_prefix) for 90% of observed routes with a confidence score and estimated token delta.
Prescriptions surfaced in Console under a 'Cost Guardian' panel with review buttons: Accept, Edit+Accept, Reject, Schedule.
Policy engine can evaluate an allowlist/denylist and tier map; policies prevent applying aggressive changes to denylisted customers or routes in P0/P1 SLA tiers.
Apply flow supports dry-run mode (no runtime changes) that simulates expected cost/latency impact using historical traces.

Canary rollout applies changes to 1-5% of traffic for a configurable window; rollback automatically triggers if p95 latency increases by >15% or error rate increases by >0.5 percentage points or quality regression detected by eval set.
Automatic rollback executes within 10 minutes of detecting a violation and publishes an incident note and telemetry snapshot to the Console.
End-to-end tests covering: prescription generation, policy blocking, dry-run accuracy within 10% of observed delta, canary success path, and rollback path.
Design doc and API spec linked; at least one customer pilot onboarded and feedback collected.
progress_updates: 2026-02-26 - Kickoff: scope agreed with PM and Design; selected initial pilot customers (2 sandbox tenants + internal load tests).
2026-03-02 - Prototype: rule-based prescription engine created that suggests batch_size and cache_ttl using route token distribution histograms.
2026-03-08 - Policy: policy engine extended with tier map and denylist evaluation; added API v1 to evaluate decisions without applying.
2026-03-11 - Canary harness: built simple canary toggle in runtime-1.22; hooked p95 and error ingestion to the detector service.
2026-03-13 - QA: dry-run simulation added; preliminary results show estimated token savings aligning within 12% of replay for non-chat routes.
